name: Parking Meters
description: Installation, removal, and hours of operation for parking meters across the city.
title_keywords: hours of operation for parking meters
summary: The most contested citywide item was the transfer of ownership of Chicago Parking Meters LLC to Stonepeak Partners LP (SO2026-0025407), which received a subject-matter Committee on Finance hearing on 2026-06-25 [1][3][4] and further discussion on 2026-09-24 covering revenue impacts, divestiture, and curb-management flexibility [2][7], before City Council passed it 46 Yea / 3 Nay on 2026-09-29. A related ordinance (O2026-0029681) adding Section 2-32-385 allocating metered parking concession payments among City pension funds passed 44 Yea / 6 Nay on 2026-11-02, with debate over whether the roughly $75 million in payments should supplement pension contributions or balance the budget [5][6]. Routine meter establishment and amendment ordinances passed unanimously across the year: SO2025-0021555 (49-0, 2025-12-10), SO2026-0023810 (50-0, 2026-03-18), SO2026-0025225 (50-0, 2026-05-20), SO2026-0026259 (49-0, 2026-06-17), SO2026-0026841 (49-0, 2026-07-15), SO2026-0029397 (49-0, 2026-10-14), and O2026-0028790 amending meter hours of operation (49-0, 2026-10-14). Ward 35 meter-removal amendments (O2026-0028251) were on the Pedestrian and Traffic Safety agenda for 2026-09-15 [10][11]; their final disposition is not shown in this trail. The Third Amendment to the concession agreement was executed following the ownership-transfer approval [12].
one_line: Council approved CPM ownership transfer to Stonepeak (46-3) and pension allocation of meter payments (44-6), alongside routine meter ordinances.
